name: Clue
tagline: Period and cycle tracker that logs symptoms and predicts your next period, ovulation window and PMS.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of a cycle tracker is a calendar, a list of symptom tags, and arithmetic over your last few cycles. An agent can produce a local PWA that logs periods, computes average cycle and luteal length, and projects the next few periods and fertile windows in a single sitting, and for a lot of people that is the whole product. What does not fall out of one session is the phone-shaped part: dependable reminders when the app is closed, encrypted sync across devices, Apple Health and Google Fit hooks, and a widget. Clue also leans hard on editorial and research content, plus a privacy posture that is a real reason people picked it over the competition. Build it if you want your cycle data in a file you own, not because the prediction math is hard.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first installable web app where you tap days on a calendar to log bleeding, symptoms and moods, and it predicts upcoming periods and fertile windows from your own history.
requirements: A browser and a static host, or just localhost
Optional: add to home screen for app-like use
whatYouLose: Reliable background notifications and lock screen reminders
Encrypted multi-device sync and a recoverable backup if your phone dies
Apple Health and Google Fit integration
Prediction models tuned on millions of logged cycles instead of your last three
The science-reviewed content library and condition specific guidance
moatNotes: For a category this sensitive, trust in the company holding the data is doing more work than the algorithm. A local file you control competes on exactly that axis.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because tracking only works if it happens every day, and daily habits live or die on friction. Clue is already installed, already reminds you, already survives a phone upgrade, and already has years of your history in it. The paid tier buys deeper analysis and content rather than the calendar itself, and the calendar itself is the part you could rebuild. Most people are paying for continuity and for not having to think about backups.
notes: The math is a moving average with extra steps; the product is the habit around it.
prompt:
Build a local-first period and cycle tracker as an installable web app. No accounts, no backend, no analytics, no network calls at all.

Stack, pick exactly this:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage
- date-fns for date math
- vite-plugin-pwa for the service worker and manifest

Data model in Dexie:
- dayLogs: date (YYYY-MM-DD, primary key), flow ('none'|'spotting'|'light'|'medium'|'heavy'), symptoms (string array), moods (string array), note (string)
- settings: single row with defaultCycleLength, defaultPeriodLength, theme

Features that are in scope:
- Month calendar view as the home screen. Tap a day to open a bottom sheet for logging flow, symptoms (cramps, headache, bloating, tender breasts, acne, fatigue, nausea, back pain), moods (happy, calm, sensitive, irritable, anxious, low), and a free text note.
- Color the calendar: logged period days, predicted period days (outlined, not filled), predicted fertile window, and today's ring.
- Derive cycles from consecutive runs of non-'none' flow days: a new cycle starts on the first bleeding day after at least 2 dry days. Compute cycle lengths, period lengths, and the mean and standard deviation of each.
- Predict the next 3 periods using the median of the last 6 cycle lengths, falling back to settings defaults when there is less than 2 cycles of history. Estimate ovulation at 14 days before the next predicted period and mark a fertile window of ovulation minus 5 through ovulation plus 1.
- Show a prediction confidence label derived from the variability of past cycles, and state plainly in the UI that these are estimates and not contraception.
- Insights page: average cycle length, average period length, shortest and longest cycle, current cycle day, days until next predicted period, and a simple bar chart of the last 12 cycle lengths.
- Export all data to a JSON file and import it back, with a merge-by-date strategy.
- Local reminder toggle using the Notification API while the app is open, and be explicit in the UI that background reminders are not supported.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, cloud sync, sharing, pregnancy mode, health platform integrations, any content library.

UI: mobile-first, thumb-reachable, large tap targets, dark mode by default, three bottom tabs (Calendar, Insights, Settings). Include a Settings toggle for a discreet app name and icon label.

Seed the database with 4 months of plausible sample cycles behind a 'load sample data' button in Settings, and a 'delete everything' button with a confirm step. Write a README covering how to run it, how to install it to a phone home screen, and where the data physically lives.
